headword: {遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}
reading: いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ

definitions.explanation: An office or counter at a station, airport, public facility, or police jurisdiction where items lost by the public are received, held, and returned to their owners. The formal term seen on signs at train stations and on railway websites.

examples.japanese: {遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}はどこですか。
{駅|えき}の{遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}に{問|と}い{合|あ}わせてみてください。
examples.english: Please try contacting the station's lost-and-found office.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}に{傘|かさ}を{忘|わす}れてしまったので、{遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}に{電話|でんわ}した。
examples.english: I left my umbrella on the train, so I called the lost-and-found office.

examples.japanese: {空港|くうこう}の{遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}で、なくした{財布|さいふ}が{見|み}つかったという{連絡|れんらく}があった。
examples.english: The airport lost-and-found office contacted me to say that the wallet I had lost had been found.

notes:
Composed of {遺失物|いしつぶつ} (lost article) and {取扱所|とりあつかいじょ} (handling office, counter). The formal, signage-style term for what is commonly called a 'lost and found' in English.

USAGE:
Seen on signage and on official websites of railway companies ({JR}、{東京|とうきょう}メトロ、etc.), airports, and police stations. In spoken Japanese, speakers often use shorter variants like {遺失物|いしつぶつ}センター or {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}センター.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駅|えき}の{遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}: the station lost-and-found
- {遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}に{問|と}い{合|あ}わせる: to inquire at the lost-and-found office
- {遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}に{届|とど}ける: to hand in / turn in (a found item) at the lost-and-found
- {遺失物取扱所|いしつぶつとりあつかいじょ}に{保管|ほかん}される: to be kept at the lost-and-found

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}センター: lost-and-found center — the more everyday term, common at railway companies' consumer-facing websites
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}センター: lost-property center — near-synonym; same scope, slightly more formal register
- {落|お}とし{物|もの}{保管所|ほかんじょ}: found-items storage — emphasizes holding items until claimed
- {拾得物|しゅうとくぶつ}: found article — the legal counterpart of {遺失物|いしつぶつ}, referring to the item from the finder's perspective
